source.excerpt: Resistance to tyranny is obedience to God.
trail: The fetched 1874 trial account records Anthony using the words while refusing her unjust fine. She introduces them as an old revolutionary maxim, so the primary record verifies her use, not her authorship. Wikiquote makes the same distinction. The trial account ↗
Wikiquote records Anthony’s use and warns against crediting her with originating the slogan. Use versus invention ↗

author.name: Susan B. Anthony
author.heading: About Susan B. Anthony
author.bio: Anthony was an American campaigner for women’s voting rights. Her trial following her vote in the 1872 election became a prominent occasion for arguing that women were entitled to political citizenship.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Anthony used the maxim while refusing to accept the legitimacy of punishment for voting. Her own reply identifies it as an older revolutionary maxim, so the trial record documents her use rather than her invention of the phrase.
